clue.text: Wrestling club that might get you hooked

parts.note: grappling is the hand-to-hand struggle of wrestlers
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A wrestling club advertises itself as the kind of place you will become addicted to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrestling club' reads as a gym; it splits into a sport and a golf club, and 'hooked' turns from addiction to a literal hook.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a grapnel, a multi-pronged hooked device thrown to catch hold of ships or ledges, so it snags whatever it reaches.

clue.text: They're usually concealed in smoking jackets

definitions.text: They're usually concealed in smoking jackets

parts.words: They're usually concealed in smoking jackets
parts.note: both cannabis cigarettes, hidden for smoking, and short double-breasted jackets worn by sailors

explanation.surface: Someone keeps illicit things tucked away in the pockets of a gentleman's lounging jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cannabis joints, which a user would hide; the word also names a type of jacket, giving the double reading.

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
to lay something is to place it down

explanation.surface: A request for a peaceful spot where one can enjoy oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: amusement or recreation, as in doing something just for the sake of it.

clue.text: Sporting poet has a grand finish

indicators.note: the poet has the next letter attached after him, closing the word

parts.note: Philip Larkin was an English poet
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A poet who plays sport rounds things off splendidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish' says the G for grand comes at the end, after the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Larking about means playing or frolicking, the old sense of sporting as making merry.

parts.note: five-cent coins made of metal are fed into slot machines to work them in the US

explanation.surface: Seems to ask who runs the metalworking machines in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: US five-cent coins, named after the metal they contain, used to start vending and slot machines.

indicators.note: providing some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An island retreat offers some spiritual inspiration through austere living.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across inspirat-ION A-scetically.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Hebridean isle off Scotland's west coast, famous for its monastery founded by St Columba.

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of prove to could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone might succeed in demonstrating their superiority.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above or surpass, i.e. to be higher or better than others.

clue.text: It's cheap, and any number can get it apparently

definitions.meaning: something selling for very little money, a bargain

definitions.text: any number can get it apparently
definitions.meaning: a number is also a song, so any number literally sets off after a tune

explanation.surface: Something inexpensive enough that anyone at all can obtain it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a piece of music, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being sold at a very low price, as goods knocked down at auction.

parts.note: a sledge is a vehicle for travelling over snow
hammers means hits or strikes

explanation.surface: Industrial action by transport workers wins the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' looks like walkouts but means blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy long-handled tools used to pound and smash things, so they are things that beat.

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so in and opera are jumbled

explanation.surface: An outdoor dance sequence performed within an opera production.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco is Italian-derived for outdoors, under the sky.

clue.text: Hide at one time found in California

indicators.note: found in places the former-time word within the state abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is a common abbreviation for the state of California
once means formerly, at one time

explanation.surface: An animal hide was once discovered in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like an animal skin, but it is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to keep out of sight or cover up.

indicators.note: awkward signals the letters of ones are in an ungainly order to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Difficult people cast votes against a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes against a motion, as counted in Parliament when ayes face the other side.

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of evict are running out of control and get reordered

explanation.surface: An instruction to throw out an untamed, foul-smelling feline.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat-like mammal known for its musky scent glands, used in perfume.

indicators.note: cuts shortens the swotting word, lopping its ending off

parts.note: swotting is British slang for studying hard

explanation.surface: A student's poker games eat into their revision time.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety of poker in which some cards are dealt face up.

indicators.note: wayward suggests letters straying from their proper order

explanation.surface: Wonders what the future holds for unfaithful wives.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: prospects are vistas or outlooks, as is a set of scenes seen from a height.

clue.text: Prepared to study before end of day

indicators.note: before places the study word ahead of the final letter

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of day

explanation.surface: A student has prepared by studying until the day is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: set or primed to act.

clue.text: Trying to get something from the bank?

definitions.text: Trying to get something from the bank?

parts.words: Trying to get something from the bank?
parts.note: an angler on a riverbank tries to catch something, not a customer at a money bank

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a customer attempting a withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: Angling, often done from a riverbank; also seeking information indirectly.

parts.note: sounds like the top rank of clergy but means the tallest physical part of the building

explanation.surface: Appears to ask for the most senior post in the ecclesiastical hierarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering tower atop a church building, its loftiest point.

indicators.note: afresh says the letters of we learn are set out anew

explanation.surface: Starting over, we pick up our studies once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning a fresh start or revival, though the definition reads as a verb form.

parts.note: read as an instruction, to foster a child is to raise and care for it

explanation.definitionFit: To rear and encourage the growth of a young person, which is what fostering does.

clue.text: What a policeman does to a criminal is hair-raising!

definitions.text: What a policeman does to a criminal

explanation.surface: An arrest described as a frightening experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hair-raising' usually means terrifying; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb for imprisoning; also, taken literally, tresses going upward.

parts.note: made means created
I is the Roman numeral one
RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A wine produced by a single painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from the Portuguese island of the same name.

parts.note: the people of the Isle of Man have a three-legged emblem, so they are a race tied to three legs

explanation.surface: Looks like the sack-race style event at school sports days.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, has a three-legged triskelion on its flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of the Isle of Man, a people whose national symbol has three legs.

clue.text: Threatens to finish in bad spirits

indicators.note: in places the finish word inside the devils

parts.note: imps are small mischievous devils
end means finish

explanation.surface: Someone's ill temper threatens to bring things to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad spirits' reads as a gloomy mood, but it means little devils.
explanation.definitionFit: To impend is to loom or hang over as imminent danger.

clue.text: Kind and good man with a heart of gold

definitions.text: good man with a heart of gold
definitions.meaning: a decent fellow, as in calling someone a good one

explanation.surface: Describes a warm-hearted, generous man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun meaning type.
explanation.definitionFit: Means a type or class, and in 'a good ...' a likeable person.

clue.text: School's head hasn't the power, being poorly supplied

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of School's

parts.note: can't means is not able, lacks the power

explanation.surface: A head teacher lacks authority because the school is under-resourced.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: meagre or barely sufficient.

indicators.note: backs here means goes back, so the charts word is read in reverse

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Someone supports schemes for sending out unsolicited post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' looks like supports; it turns MAPS around.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited bulk email, the electronic equivalent of junk post.

clue.text: Composer drops in for a bit of pork

indicators.note: drops means the composer loses the two letters of in

parts.note: Chopin was the Polish composer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer pops in to get some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops in' looks like 'visits'; here the composer drops the letters IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of meat, such as a pork cutlet including a rib.

clue.text: River a group of sailors love

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Some sailors are fond of a particular river.
explanation.definitionFit: The river that flows through Florence and Pisa in Tuscany.

parts.note: zeros literally stand for nothing in counting

explanation.surface: Describes people of no importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeros, the symbols that represent no quantity at all.

clue.text: Itinerant craftsman and ancient poetic character

definitions.meaning: a seafarer who travels about in a craft, meaning a boat
the Ancient one of Coleridge's Rime

explanation.surface: A wandering artisan who is also an old literary figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftsman' is a man of craft, meaning vessels, not skilled handiwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor, a man of ships; also the old seaman in Coleridge's famous poem.

clue.text: Offer hospitality to all, though a cold thing to do in winter

definitions.text: though a cold thing to do in winter
definitions.meaning: literally leaving your doors unclosed lets the chill in

explanation.surface: Generosity to guests has a chilly drawback in the cold months.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for welcoming guests at any time; read literally, leaving the doors ajar.
